schema.name: working_footage
schema.subject: 00-WORKING/Videos/ — July 2026 Pamir shoot
schema.note: Container/timing/colour measured on all clips. signalstats, scdet and cropdetect NOT run — see WORKING_FOOTAGE.md section 5.

motion_classification.method: GPS haversine speed + bearing-delta turn rate, 0.5s sampling
motion_classification.confidence: inferred — NOT cross-checked against visual review

exposure_signal.method: cv2 decode -> BGR2GRAY -> scoring_exposure._clipped_fraction, 2 frames per clip, 28 clips (14 HLG / 14 SDR)
exposure_signal.finding: HLG-vs-SDR bias hypothesis REFUTED as material: direction real, magnitude negligible (<=0.0017 on composite). The actionable defect is that exposure is near-constant -- LOW_CLIP_THRESHOLD=5 / HIGH_CLIP_THRESHOLD=250 measure sensor clipping, which this footage does not exhibit, while carrying 25% of composite weight.
exposure_signal.unresolved: clean HLG->bt709 tonemap control not run; this ffmpeg build lacks the zscale filter

signal_discrimination.method: 15 x 720p 3s proxy segments, 3 frames each, sampled across the library
signal_discrimination.note: 9 proxy encodes failed silently; sample skews HLG

exposure_score_span.finding: occupies 1.8% of the [0,1] scale it is weighted 25% on

redundancy_spearman.note: no other pair exceeded |rho|=0.8; saturation/contrast/midtone/dynamic_range are mutually independent and independent of sharpness

caveats: 3 frames from one mid-clip window: between-clip separation only, says nothing about within-clip variation which is what segment scoring needs
sharpness_laplacian is NOT scale-invariant; values from 720p proxies are not transferable to 4K
two ratio metrics (IQR/median, p90/p10) were tried and discarded: both divide by a near-zero quantity and ranked the most inert signal as most discriminating
